why: Both moved the same two clients with the same diff and were honest about embeddings, but A drove the real entry point end to end and found that the product's only user-facing path (OpenAIAgent.astream_chat) silently drops every tool call, so SEC Insights currently answers every financial question with its "Sorry, I don't have an answer" fallback — diagnosed to the chunk-1 gate, reproduced with no Router in the path, fixed and measured before/after. That single finding outranks every cost lever in either report and also undercuts B's turn-level arithmetic, which prices a five-to-twenty-call pipeline that never executes in production async streaming; B's Router-side design is genuinely better engineered, which is why the margin is slight rather than clear.
A_best: Found, diagnosed, fixed and measured a pre-existing llama-index bug that makes the whole product return an empty answer — correctly ranked above all cost and routing levers, with the monkeypatch liability named and sequenced behind a FunctionAgent migration (i7).
B_best: Per-workload LLM roles with explicit Router feature labels (sec_chat_answer / sec_rag / sec_doc_financials), verified per-feature policy matching, which makes every other lever targetable — and is what lets B put gpt-6-luna only on the RAG workload (measured -71%) instead of on the user-facing answer; pinning service_tier "default" against an account default that measurably serves Flex is the sharpest Router-specific catch in either report.
A_worst: Declared feature labels "not stable enough to key a policy on" and so built only global defaults — which B disproved — leaving A's model swap (i4) applied to every role including the streaming answer, recommended off two prompts with no mention of latency, when B measured the same model at ~2.3x slower on an app where every call sits inside the user's wait.
B_worst: Never drove handle_chat_message end to end, so it missed that the product is currently broken and reported turn-level call counts, costs and latency chains for a path that does not run; its llm-roles-derived branches also carry an outside-check flag for removing the OPENAI_API_KEY reference, which embeddings still require.
